title: Rogue Network Bridge — Electrical Room B

fields.organization: North Coast Regional Airport Authority — IT & Cybersecurity
fields.location: Electrical Room B, Concourse B, Level 2
fields.summary: During a physical inspection of Electrical Room B, a modified TP-Link wireless router was discovered hidden behind the UPS battery backup unit. The device is connected via USB to the UPS power feed and to Port 23 on the Cisco Catalyst 2960 switch. The device is broadcasting a hidden SSID and has two external antennas. Signal strength analysis indicates it can be accessed from the Concourse B parking structure. The device has been connected for approximately 30 minutes and is actively bridging to the Concourse B operational VLAN. MAC address: 50:C7:BF:XX:XX:XX (TP-Link OUI). No logs or traffic traces have been extracted yet. The device remains in place for forensic preservation.

findings.notes: No damage or tampering observed. Device is physically attached behind unit.
Cable to device shows no external port damage. Port status shows active link and up.
Modified TP-Link model, 2.4 GHz only. Hidden SSID active. Antenna pattern suggests directional access from Concourse B parking lot.
USB cable tapped into UPS power feed. No external power source visible.
Pending network team verification.

findings.item: Physical access log for Door S-4
findings.notes: Confirmed via PACS log: clone entry at 07:38.
No camera inside room. Corridor camera only captures entry/exit.
Pending verification by IT network team.
No biometric lock present. Physical key not required for entry.
50:C7:BF:XX:XX:XX — matches known TP-Link OUI. No known device in inventory with this MAC.

actionsTaken: Photographed device and surrounding area using device camera (IMG_20261022_0834_01 to IMG_20261022_0834_04)
Documented MAC address and port connection
Secured scene with tape and signage: 'DO NOT TOUCH — FORENSIC EVIDENCE'
Notified IT Lead and Security IC via radio at 08:34
Confirmed device remains powered and connected for forensic analysis
recommendations: Immediately isolate Concourse B operational VLAN from core network
Conduct full switch port audit on Cisco 2960 for unauthorized MAC addresses
Trace all traffic from Port 23 using packet capture tools
Begin forensic imaging of SEC-SVR-01 and NCIA-PACS-CORE for related access logs
Deploy security team to monitor parking structure near Concourse B for suspicious activity
fields.photosNote: 4 photos attached: IMG_20261022_0834_01 (device view), IMG_20261022_0834_02 (port connection), IMG_20261022_0834_03 (antenna orientation), IMG_20261022_0834_04 (device behind UPS)

instructorNote: This is the critical puzzle piece: the rogue device is a bridge, not a direct access point. The players must now recognize that physical access to a network room enabled a cyber foothold. Watch for IT to request network logs and switch configs.
